payload.feature: brokkr export gains --redact: a sanitized copy for publishable fixtures. Today export writes the canonical NDJSON journal verbatim, and verbatim exports embed operator-machine detail — absolute paths and usernames in effect/started driver commands, checkpoint targets, and workdir fields (the review of the fold-arm slice recorded exactly this residual: the committed fixture is the one artifact in the public repo carrying /home/<user> paths). Scope: (1) 'brokkr export --run <id> --redact' writes, ALONGSIDE nothing else changed, a sanitized variant: every absolute filesystem path in event payload string fields is rewritten to a stable placeholder that preserves distinctness (the same original path always becomes the same placeholder, distinct paths stay distinct, e.g. [path-1], [path-2]), usernames inside such paths never survive, and everything else — event structure, seqs, hashes need not re-verify (see 3) — is untouched. (2) The redacted file and its manifest are UNMISTAKABLY marked as redacted (filename suffix and a manifest field), because a sanitized copy that could pass as verbatim evidence would be a forgery — decision 0019 law three's spirit applies to machines too. (3) Honesty about the chain: redaction breaks the recorded event hashes by construction; the redacted manifest must SAY so (a field naming the redaction and that hash verification applies only to the verbatim export), and 'brokkr export' WITHOUT --redact stays byte-identical to today. (4) Default output naming keeps the run id; --redact adds the marked suffix. Tests must pin: placeholder stability and distinctness; no username or absolute path survives anywhere in the redacted NDJSON; the redacted manifest carries the marking fields; the verbatim path is unchanged by the flag's existence; and a fixture-sized journal round-trips through redaction deterministically (same input, same output). CI enforces exact coverage — keep the gate green.

result.notes: brokkr export --redact implemented: forge_store::redact_export rewrites every absolute path in event payload strings to stable [path-N] placeholders (journal-wide table: same path same placeholder, distinct stay distinct) and scrubs usernames harvested from /home|/Users paths wherever they reappear bare ([user-N]) — the fixture records the operator by OS username outside any path, so path-only redaction would have leaked it. Redacted pair is marked by .redacted. filename suffix and manifest fields redacted:true + redaction{scheme,hashes} stating hash verification applies only to the verbatim export; verbatim output byte-identical with or without the flag (pinned by test). Tests pin placeholder stability/distinctness, no /home or username anywhere in redacted NDJSON, manifest marks, fixture round-trip determinism with envelope fields untouched. cargo test --workspace green (36/36 suites); fmt and clippy -D warnings clean; exact coverage verified at literal 100%: 11322/11322 lines, 1700/1700 branches, 988/988 functions via cargo +nightly llvm-cov --branch. Committed 1021dc4 (--no-gpg-sign per operator amend-sign flow), not pushed.

1) cargo test --workspace: all 33 suites ok — 552 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (includes machine proof and differential corpus parity tests; forge_core lib 166 passed, forge_cli 117 passed, forge_view 47 passed, forge_bridge 46+52 passed, plus doc-tests incl. the Secret compile-fail). 2) cargo run -p forge-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: compiled clean under the constitutional lint — digest 638a4efa2c4a425af0d709be626dfb5dcf0a84c6b1304de0bb830384f28ea29f, all five seats resolved with empty notices/skipped, engine 0.4.0.

Reviewed 1021dc4 (redact_export in forge-store, --redact in forge-cli, tests in both). Correctness: sound — placeholder stability/distinctness via insertion-ordered table is right; determinism holds (no HashMap iteration reaches output; user numbering is by raw-text first appearance); verbatim byte-identity with and without the flag is pinned; re-serialization matches export_ndjson's canonical Value form (no preserve_order feature); blank-line drop, payload-free lines, URL authorities, ratios, and username token bounds are all pinned. Fixture test confirms no /home or username survives and every envelope field outside payload is untouched. Manifest copied into the redacted manifest is digests + relative bundle filenames only — no leak there; object keys are not redacted but no real journal payload keys carry paths. cargo test --workspace: all green; clippy: clean. FIX APPLIED (d9190d4, doc-only): the recognizer is /-rooted (POSIX) only, and Brokkr ships a Windows release binary — a Windows-recorded journal (C:\Users\<name>\...) would come back from --redact marked sanitized with the username intact, silently. Extending the recognizer is beyond a reviewer-sized change, so the rustdoc and the manifest's redaction.scheme field now state the POSIX bound explicitly, converting silent false assurance into a declared limitation. RESIDUALS: (1) [low, security] Windows drive-letter paths are not redacted — now documented, still unimplemented; a Windows operator publishing a redacted export leaks paths/username. (2) [info, security] //-rooted paths and file:///home/... URLs survive verbatim (the //-authority carve-out is pinned as intended); a home path behind file:// would leak, contrived in real journals. (3) [info, security] non-ASCII usernames: is_path_char is ASCII-only, so /home/józef truncates the placeholder at the first non-ASCII char and the username tail survives; POSIX portable usernames are ASCII. Coverage gate: verify phase already ruled VERIFY-PASS; the doc fix adds no lines/branches. No high/critical finding — no security-hold.
